_provenance.title: National curriculum in England: languages programmes of study
_provenance.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
_provenance.scope: Statutory programme-of-study statements only (the 'Pupils should be taught' lists), verbatim. Non-statutory notes and guidance, aims, purpose of study and appendices are not included.

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: listen attentively to spoken language and show understanding by joining in and responding

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: explore the patterns and sounds of language through songs and rhymes and link the spelling, sound and meaning of words

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: engage in conversations; ask and answer questions; express opinions and respond to those of others; seek clarification and help*

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: speak in sentences, using familiar vocabulary, phrases and basic language structures

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: develop accurate pronunciation and intonation so that others understand when they are reading aloud or using familiar words and phrases*

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: present ideas and information orally to a range of audiences*

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: read carefully and show understanding of words, phrases and simple writing

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: appreciate stories, songs, poems and rhymes in the language

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: broaden their vocabulary and develop their ability to understand new words that are introduced into familiar written material, including through using a dictionary

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: write phrases from memory, and adapt these to create new sentences, to express ideas clearly

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: describe people, places, things and actions orally* and in writing

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: understand basic grammar appropriate to the language being studied, including (where relevant): feminine, masculine and neuter forms and the conjugation of high-frequency verbs; key features and patterns of the language; how to apply these, for instance, to build sentences; and how these differ from or are similar to English

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: identify and use tenses or other structures which convey the present, past, and future as appropriate to the language being studied

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: use and manipulate a variety of key grammatical structures and patterns, including voices and moods, as appropriate

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: develop and use a wide-ranging and deepening vocabulary that goes beyond their immediate needs and interests, allowing them to give and justify opinions and take part in discussion about wider issues

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: use accurate grammar, spelling and punctuation

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: listen to a variety of forms of spoken language to obtain information and respond appropriately

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: transcribe words and short sentences that they hear with increasing accuracy

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: initiate and develop conversations, coping with unfamiliar language and unexpected responses, making use of important social conventions such as formal modes of address

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: express and develop ideas clearly and with increasing accuracy, both orally and in writing

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: speak coherently and confidently, with increasingly accurate pronunciation and intonation

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: read and show comprehension of original and adapted materials from a range of different sources, understanding the purpose, important ideas and details, and provide an accurate English translation of short, suitable material

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: read literary texts in the language [such as stories, songs, poems and letters] to stimulate ideas, develop creative expression and expand understanding of the language and culture

statements.subject: languages
statements.text: write prose using an increasingly wide range of grammar and vocabulary, write creatively to express their own ideas and opinions, and translate short written text accurately into the foreign language
